title: Medulin Cost Guide 2027: Prices for Stays, Food, Transport
metaDescription: Medulin 2027 cost guide: apartment and hotel rates, meals, coffee, beer, parking, bus fares, tourist tax and daily budgets, all in euros.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Medulin Cost?

Medulin sits on the southern tip of Istria and is cheaper than Split or Dubrovnik, mainly on accommodation and dining. Budget travelers who self-cater spend about €70–€100 per person per day. Mid-range visitors with a 3-star hotel or a good apartment and restaurant dinners spend €120–€200 per person per day. Most of the swing comes from the month of travel.

All prices below are in euros and are typical ranges. Exact rates depend on the dates, the property and how early you book.

## Accommodation Prices in Medulin

### Apartments

Private apartments are the standard way to stay in Medulin. Rates vary a lot by season:

- **Peak (July–August):** €90–€180 per night for a studio or one-bedroom; €160–€350 for a two-bedroom sleeping four.
- **Shoulder (May–June, September–October):** €60–€120 for a studio or one-bedroom; €100–€220 for a two-bedroom.
- **Off-season (November–April):** about €45–€80 for a studio or one-bedroom.

A two-bedroom apartment for a full peak-season week often costs €600–€1,050 at the lower end of the market. Many hosts set minimum stays of 5–7 nights in July and August.

### Hotels

The main hotel names include Park Plaza Belvedere Medulin, Arena Hotel Holiday and Hotel Arcus. Mid-range 3–4 star hotels cost about €150–€280 per night in shoulder season and €220–€400 or more in peak summer. Many offer half-board, which can be good value when restaurant dinners cost €30–€50 per person. Newer properties price above the budget tier.

### Campsites and guesthouses

Medulin is known for its campsites. A standard pitch for two adults costs €25–€45 per night in July and August and €15–€25 in May, June and September. Guesthouse doubles with a private bathroom start around €40–€70 outside peak weeks.

### Tourist tax

Medulin's tourist tax is €1.60 per adult per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.10 the rest of the year. Children under 12 are generally exempt and ages 12–18 pay 50%. Private renters sometimes list it separately, so confirm whether it is in the quoted price.

## Food and Drink Prices

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Espresso or macchiato | €2.00–€3.00 |
| Cappuccino or latte | €3.00–€4.00 |
| Draft beer, 0.5L | €3.50–€5.00 |
| Glass of wine | €4.00–€7.00 |
| Konoba meal (budget) | about €18 per person |
| Mid-range restaurant dinner | €30–€50 per person |
| Groceries, daily self-catering | about €10 per person |

Self-catering with supermarket groceries plus one konoba meal every few days is what keeps a budget trip near €70 per person per day. Lunch at a café or a self-made lunch runs about €10–€20.

Skip the harbor-front tables for dinner if price matters. Konobas one or two streets back from the promenade charge noticeably less for the same grilled fish and pasta, and locals eat there.

## Transport Costs

### From Pula Airport

Pula Airport is about 10–14km from Medulin. A private taxi costs around €25–€30 on fixed-rate transfers, and up to €35–€45 for metered or peak rides. A shuttle bus to Medulin takes about 40 minutes. A single airport-to-Pula shuttle ticket is €6. Port of Pula and Pula train station are both about 13km away, with taxis at roughly €15–€20.

### Local buses

The Medulin–Pula bus costs about €2.50–€3.50 one way. Buses run every 30–60 minutes in peak season (June–September) from Pula's main bus station.

### Car rental, fuel and parking

A compact rental car costs about €45–€65 per day in July and August, with fuel around €1.80 per liter. Paid parking runs €1–€2.50 per hour, or €10–€20 for a full day. The large lot near Bijeca beach is paid. Free spots exist farther from the promenade but need a walk. Many apartments include private parking, which saves €10–€20 a day in summer.

A car is worth it only if Istria beyond Medulin is on the plan. Within town, walking and cycling are enough. Entry to Cape Kamenjak costs roughly €10–20 per car depending on the season, and is free on foot or by bike.

### Boat trips

Water taxi return trips to Levan Island cost about €15–€20 per person.

## Sample Daily Budgets

### Budget: €70–€100 per person per day

Campsite pitch or basic apartment shared between two, groceries, one café stop, beach days, a bus ride to Pula.

### Mid-range: €120–€200 per person per day

An apartment or 3-star hotel (€60–€100 per person when shared), breakfast at the accommodation, lunch for €10–€20, dinner for €30–€50, a rental car on some days.

### Comfort: above €200 per person per day

4-star hotel in July or August, restaurant dinners every night, boat excursions and a car.

## Cheapest Time to Visit Medulin

May, June and September cut accommodation costs by roughly 30–40% against July and August, and the sea is still warm enough for swimming in June and September. Off-season apartment prices drop to €45–€80, but many beach bars and seasonal restaurants close. Book peak-season apartments several months ahead to get the better rates.

## Free and Low-Cost Things to Do

- Swimming and sunbathing on Bijeca and other pebble and rock beaches
- Walking and cycling the coastal paths of the Medulin Riviera
- Walking into Cape Kamenjak on foot or by bike (no vehicle fee)
- Visiting the Vižula archaeological site, a short walk from the town

## Money-Saving Tips

- Choose accommodation with free parking if arriving by car.
- Use bank ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion at machines and card terminals.
- Carry small euro notes and coins for parking machines and small purchases.
- Shop at supermarkets for beach food, and keep dinners out for konobas away from the harbor.
- Ask if the tourist tax is included before paying a deposit.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Answers are in the FAQ section below.

faq.question: Is Medulin expensive?
faq.answer: Medulin is cheaper than Split or Dubrovnik, especially for accommodation and dining. It is still pricey in July and August, when apartments can cost €90–€180 per night and hotels €220–€400 or more.

faq.question: How much money do you need per day in Medulin?
faq.answer: Plan on €70–€100 per person for a budget trip with self-catering, and €120–€200 per person for mid-range travel. Costs fall in May, June and September.

faq.question: How much is the tourist tax in Medulin?
faq.answer: The tax is €1.60 per adult per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.10 from October to March. Children under 12 are generally exempt, and ages 12–18 pay half.

faq.question: How much is a taxi from Pula Airport to Medulin?
faq.answer: A taxi costs about €25–€30 on fixed-rate transfers and up to €35–€45 on other bookings. The trip is 12–14km and takes about 20 minutes.

faq.question: How much does parking cost in Medulin?
faq.answer: Paid parking is typically €1–€2.50 per hour and €10–€20 for a full day in summer. Choosing an apartment with private parking avoids most of this cost.

faq.question: What is the cheapest month to visit Medulin?
faq.answer: November to April has the lowest prices, with apartments from €45–€80 per night, but many seasonal venues close. May, June and September combine moderate prices with open restaurants and warm weather.

faq.question: How much does a coffee or beer cost in Medulin?
faq.answer: An espresso costs €2–€3 and a cappuccino €3–€4. A 0.5L draft beer is €3.50–€5 and a glass of wine €4–€7.
